proposed_comments.title: Use complete Windows argument escaping and add regression coverage
proposed_comments.body:
### Use complete Windows argument escaping and add regression coverage

**Severity:** `high`

The unquoted `%1` branch only escapes embedded double quotes; it does not double backslashes before embedded quotes or before the closing delimiter, so paths ending in a backslash or containing backslashes immediately before quotes can still change the argument delivered to the browser. Please use a standard Windows command-line argument-quoting routine and add focused tests for quoted and unquoted `%1`, multi-word input, embedded quotes, trailing backslashes, and null input. This is a general review note rather than an apply-ready inline suggestion because the safe correction requires a helper and tests outside the current one-file hunk.

confidence.rationale: The current diff directly performs ad-hoc quote replacement, while the fork-side regression tests reproduced failures for trailing backslashes and embedded quotes and the corrected helper passed targeted tests.

test_instructions: Enable PowerToys Run and configure a browser whose command pattern contains an unquoted %1 placeholder.
Run a WebSearch query containing multiple words and verify the browser receives the complete query as one argument rather than truncating after the first word.
Repeat with a query containing a trailing backslash and embedded quotes, and verify the browser command remains valid.
